title: Noetherian approximation at a flat module point
statement: Let R -> S be a finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], let M be a finitely presented S-module with its restricted R-action, and let q be a prime of S [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Assume M_q is flat over R [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then there are commutative rings A and B, a B-module N, and a commuting square A -> B, R -> S with A -> R and B -> S, such that A is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], B is finite type over A [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], N is finite over B [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], the square is a tensor-product pushout, M is isomorphic as an S-module to S tensor_B N [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and N localized at the contraction of q to B is flat over A. The A-actions are the restricted actions. The model rings and module may all be taken in the maximum of the input universes. No neighborhood or openness is asserted.

source.place: Theorem Tag 00RC, first reduction paragraph, lines 33427-33451; Lemmas Tags 00R1 and 00R6

proof.text: After transporting to a common universe if necessary, apply the simultaneous algebra-module approximation theorem (00R1). Contract q and its inverse image in R along the stage coprojections. Each stage base is finite type over the integers and thus Noetherian; the stage top rings are finite type over the bases and the modules are finite.

Localize the systems at these contracted primes. The ring colimits are the corresponding localizations of R and S. Fractions in the module colimit come from a common stage, and equal fractions are witnessed by a multiplier outside the prime and an equality which holds at a later stage. This identifies the module colimit with M_q.

Localized transitions are local since later primes contract to earlier primes. Localized rings are Noetherian local rings, and localized modules remain finite. Localize the canonical ring and module base-change isomorphisms of 00R1. The later prime complement supplies the further localization required by 00R6; tensor-localization compatibility gives its module base-change hypothesis.
Use equivalence of flatness over the base and its prime localization to apply 00R6. It gives a stage whose localized module is flat over the localized base, hence also over the unlocalized base.

Take A, B and N from that stage. The canonical limit base-change isomorphisms give the tensor pushout and M = S tensor_B N, compatible with the restricted scalar actions. Transporting these rings and the finite module to the maximum universe preserves all of the assertions.

theorem exists_noetherian_model_flat_at_prime
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {M : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.FinitePresentation S M]
    (q : PrimeSpectrum S)
    (hq : Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl M)) :
    ∃ (A B N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : CommRing B)
      (_ : Algebra A B) (_ : Algebra A R) (_ : Algebra B S) (_ : Algebra A S)
      (_ : IsScalarTower A B S) (_ : IsScalarTower A R S)
      (_ : AddCommGroup N) (_ : Module A N) (_ : Module B N)
      (_ : IsScalarTower A B N),
      IsNoetherianRing A ∧ Algebra.FiniteType A B ∧ Module.Finite B N ∧
      Algebra.IsPushout A R B S ∧ Nonempty (S ⊗[B] N ≃ₗ[S] M) ∧
      Module.Flat A
        (LocalizedModule (q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap B S)).primeCompl N)
